nearAi.baseUrl.description: NEAR AI Cloud API base URL.

nearAi.defaultModel.description: Model used for new chats. If NEAR AI doesn't offer it, the first available chat model is used. A model chosen for this project in Compare Models is used instead of this setting until you clear it there or with SovAI: Clear This Project's Model Choices.

nearAi.actionPolicy.description: How much the agent may do without asking. Every file change can be reverted from the chat.
enumDescriptions: File edits and shell commands ask first; reads and searches run automatically.
File edits run automatically; shell commands still ask unless allow-listed.

Auto approve: file edits run, and shell commands run when they pass the safety check. Clear cases are decided by fixed rules (builds, tests, and read-only git run; pushes, deletes, publishing, and credential paths ask); only commands the rules cannot decide go to a private (TEE) model, and anything it cannot clear asks.

Everything runs without asking except deny-listed commands. Writes into .git/ and SovAI's state folders, publishing and destruction still ask, and key and credential folders are refused. Use only in throwaway workspaces.

nearAi.autoInstallGsd.description: Install Open-GSD into the extension's storage the first time you run a workflow, and keep it on the latest stable release in projects set up with SovAI. Your ~/.claude setup is never touched.

enumDescriptions: Any model your rules allow; each answer shows where it ran and what was checked.
Only verified private hardware or this computer: NEAR AI private hardware, checked each time it is used, or a model on this computer.
nearAi.privacyMode.description: Where chats may run. Your organization's rules and each chat's label decide first.

nearAi.dailySpendLimitUsd.description: Stop sending NEAR AI requests once today's spend reaches this amount in USD: NEAR AI Cloud's own total for your API key when a usage reporting token is set, or this computer's spend ledger (confirmed plus pending), whichever is higher. Checked before every request and every model turn. 0 means no limit.

enumDescriptions: Today starts at midnight on this computer's clock.
nearAi.spend.dayBoundary.description: When "today" starts for spend figures and nearAi.dailySpendLimitUsd.

nearAi.spend.useNearUsageTotal.markdownDescription: Match the NEAR AI console exactly by using NEAR's own usage total for your API key (in every spend figure and for `#nearAi.dailySpendLimitUsd#`) when a usage reporting token is set; off, figures are this computer's spend ledger. The token is stored in VS Code's encrypted secret storage, never in settings. [Set usage reporting token](command:nearAi.setUsageReportingToken) · [Clear](command:nearAi.clearUsageReportingToken) · How to create one: an organization owner or admin calls `POST /v1/organizations/{org_id}/reporting-tokens` with a NEAR AI Cloud console session token (it is not in the console UI); it starts with `rpt-`.

nearAi.agent.allowCommands.description: Shell commands the agent may run without asking, matched by their leading words ("git push" covers "git push origin main", but never --force or a URL). The approval card's "Always allow" adds entries here. In Auto approve mode each part of a chained command (cd app && git push) is matched on its own; in other modes, commands that chain, redirect, or substitute always ask. The deny list is checked first. An entry whose first word is a program that can do almost anything (rm, curl, wget, ssh, sudo, node, python, bash and the other interpreters) is never honoured, because allowing it would allow almost anything.

nearAi.agent.autoAllowOutsideWorkspace.markdownDescription: In Auto approve mode, let the agent read outside this project without asking (a file elsewhere on this computer, a folder above it). Reading outside the project is what research does. It never covers writing outside the project, running a command in another folder, or anything that can send data out, and none of those is affected by this switch. The project remembers this, so the same read is not asked again.

nearAi.agent.autoAllowInstalls.markdownDescription: In Auto approve mode, let the agent install or download software without asking (a package manager install, a downloaded script). Off by default, because installing changes this machine. It never covers publishing, deleting, or reading keys, which always ask.

nearAi.agent.denyCommands.description: Shell commands the agent is never allowed to run, matched as substrings, whatever the action policy.

nearAi.teams.updateNotifications.description: Say once when a team made from a built-in project type (a project team or one of your teams) has a newer template. Update Team previews every change and asks before writing.

nearAi.agent.deepModel.description: Model for Open-GSD sub-agents in the deep tier (opus). If your provider does not offer it, the chat's model is used. A model chosen for this project in Compare Models is used instead of this setting until you clear it there or with SovAI: Clear This Project's Model Choices.

nearAi.agent.standardModel.description: Model for Open-GSD sub-agents in the standard tier (sonnet). If your provider does not offer it, the chat's model is used. A model chosen for this project in Compare Models is used instead of this setting until you clear it there or with SovAI: Clear This Project's Model Choices.

nearAi.agent.fastModel.description: Model for Open-GSD sub-agents in the fast tier (haiku). If your provider does not offer it, the chat's model is used. A model chosen for this project in Compare Models is used instead of this setting until you clear it there or with SovAI: Clear This Project's Model Choices.

nearAi.agent.safetyModel.description: Model that checks shell commands the rules cannot decide when nearAi.actionPolicy is auto. Empty uses the fast tier (nearAi.agent.fastModel). It is used only when it runs privately (in NEAR's TEE or on a local runtime); otherwise those commands ask. A model chosen for this project in Compare Models is used instead of this setting until you clear it there or with SovAI: Clear This Project's Model Choices.

nearAi.agent.maxParallelAgents.description: How many sub-agents may run at the same time. A research team of nine workstreams finishes in about the time of one workstream when this is 8 or more; the earlier default of 4, with agents that worked one part at a time, left most runs with a single request in flight.

nearAi.agent.maxParallelWorktrees.description: How many sub-agents may work in their own git worktree at the same time (each checks out the project and may build it). Counts within nearAi.agent.maxParallelAgents.

nearAi.agent.autoResumeAfterReload.description: When VS Code reloads (or code-server restarts) in the middle of an agent run, carry the run on by itself from its last saved step, with a notice in its conversation. Steps that had finished are not run again. Runs cut off more than 12 hours ago are left for you to resume.

nearAi.gsd.researchProfile.description: Research and writing projects use SovAI's research profile for Open-GSD: coarse phases, quick mode for content edits, deterministic verifier scripts in scripts/verify/, and the plan-checker only for plans that change a gate or verifier (a content-only plan's check is skipped with a note). Off: every plan is checked.

nearAi.agent.maxTurns.description: The most model turns one agent run (or sub-agent) may take before it stops and asks you to continue.

nearAi.agent.saveTranscripts.description: Save full conversations (including file contents the agent read), encrypted, in this project's git-ignored state folder (.near-ai/state) so every editor on this computer shows the same chats and they can be resumed from History. They are never committed.

nearAi.history.liveConversations.description: How many of the most recently used conversations per project stay fully open. Older ones are archived inside the project, never deleted, and reopen in full when you choose them.

nearAi.sync.intervalMinutes.description: How often, in minutes, this project syncs in the background while you are not running anything. 0 turns the background sync off. Project sync itself runs only after you turn it on (SovAI: Turn On Project Sync).

nearAi.sync.keepKeyInProject.description: Keeps this project's chat key in a private file inside the project's ignored state folder, so every editor on this computer can open the chats. Turn this off to keep the key only in each editor's secret storage; each new editor or browser then asks for the recovery code.
nearAi.sync.keepKeyInProject.markdownDescription:
Keeps this project's chat key in a private file inside the project's ignored state folder, so every editor on this computer can open the chats. Turn this off to keep the key only in each editor's secret storage; each new editor or browser then asks for the recovery code.

[Turn on project sync](command:nearAi.sync.turnOn) to keep this project on your other machines.

nearAi.agent.visionModel.description: Reads image attachments when the chat's model can't (private by default). A model chosen for this project in Compare Models is used instead of this setting until you clear it there or with SovAI: Clear This Project's Model Choices.

nearAi.agent.transcriptionModel.description: Transcribes audio attachments (private by default). A model chosen for this project in Compare Models is used instead of this setting until you clear it there or with SovAI: Clear This Project's Model Choices.

nearAi.agent.imageModel.description: Model the agent's GenerateImage tool uses (private by default). The tool is offered only when your provider lists this model. A model chosen for this project in Compare Models is used instead of this setting until you clear it there or with SovAI: Clear This Project's Model Choices.

enumDescriptions: Each image the agent makes is shown in the chat first. It is saved where the agent wanted only when you accept it; you can also ask for changes or discard it.
Images are saved where the agent wants them straight away, without showing them to you first.
nearAi.agent.imageReview.description: Whether you review each image the agent makes before it is saved in your project. While an image waits for you, the agent waits too, in every approval mode; past nearAi.agent.approvalTimeoutMinutes the run is paused on it, as on an approval, and the card stays. Only in Full auto and for a background sub-agent does the review time out at that point instead, with the draft kept and the run carrying on. Images waiting for review are kept in the project's .near-ai/drafts/images folder, which is never committed; ones left there are removed after 7 days.

nearAi.activity.retentionMinutes.description: How long the agents' prompts, replies, and tool calls are kept for Agent Activity's "Export details", in minutes. They are kept in memory only and dropped after this; the overview's counts are kept in the project's activity history.

nearAi.activity.maxMegabytes.description: The most memory those entries use, in MB. The oldest are dropped first; per-agent totals are kept.

enumDescriptions: Ask once per project before the first check.
Check every SovAI project when it opens and when its lockfiles change.
Never check automatically; the command still works after you agree.
nearAi.security.scanOnOpen.description: Check a SovAI project's dependencies and runtimes for known vulnerabilities (OSV.dev, endoflife.date) when it opens. Only package names and versions are sent.

enumDescriptions: Agents cannot search; they can still fetch pages they know.
Brave Search API (key set with SovAI: Set Up Web Search).
Tavily (key set with SovAI: Set Up Web Search).
nearAi.webSearch.provider.description: Which search provider the agents' WebSearch tool uses. Queries go to that provider.

nearAi.webSearch.searxngUrl.description: Base URL of your SearXNG instance (https, or http for localhost), with JSON output enabled.

nearAi.agent.maxRunCostUsd.description: Stops a run (the agent and all its sub-agents) once its estimated cost reaches this many US dollars; never more than what is left of nearAi.dailySpendLimitUsd. Its work is kept.

nearAi.agent.maxRunTokens.description: Stops a run (the agent and all its sub-agents) once it has used this many tokens on models without published prices; priced models are bounded by nearAi.agent.maxRunCostUsd instead. Its work is kept.

nearAi.agent.shellEnvAllow.description: Environment variables to pass to the agent's shell even though they look like credentials (for example GITHUB_TOKEN for gh). Others whose names or values look like keys, tokens, or passwords are kept out, because the agent's commands could send them to the model.

nearAi.agent.approvalTimeoutMinutes.description: How long an action in the main conversation waits for your approval before the run is paused on that step. Nothing runs while it is paused; answering whenever you are back carries on from exactly there. If nobody answers for a further day, the action is declined and the run released. 0 waits indefinitely, with no pause and no decline. Sub-agents wait nearAi.agent.subagentApprovalWaitSeconds instead and then carry on. Questions the agent asks you and images waiting for your review do the same: the run is paused on them and their card stays for you to answer, with the image draft kept. Only in Full auto (fully-autonomous) and for a sub-agent running in the background do they end at this timeout instead: the card closes as timed out, the question is answered "(no answer, timed out)", the image draft is kept, and the run carries on. 0 lets them wait indefinitely.

nearAi.agent.unattendedAutoApprove.description: In the Auto and Edits auto approval modes, sub-agents run without a card: commands the safety rules call safe (reads, read-only git, tests, lint, type checks, builds, and writes inside the sub-agent's own folder or worktree) and verification scripts inside the project that are named like a check (verify, check, gate, lint, test, typecheck, validate, audit) or named by the plan, when no agent of the run wrote or changed them (a script an agent writes during the run always asks) and they contain nothing that reaches the network, deletes, publishes, starts other programs, or touches credentials. Pushes, deletes outside the project, publishing, network commands and credential paths still ask. Ask before edits is never affected.

nearAi.agent.subagentApprovalWaitSeconds.description: How long a sub-agent's approval card waits for an answer before the sub-agent is told "awaiting approval" and carries on with other work. The card stays queued; approving it later allows that exact command for the rest of the run and tells the lead agent. The main conversation's own approvals use nearAi.agent.approvalTimeoutMinutes.

nearAi.agent.approvalTimeoutsBeforePause.description: Pause the whole run after this many approvals in a row go unanswered, with a message, instead of letting it carry on without them. Answering an approval, pressing Resume on an agent, or sending a message carries on. 0 never pauses.

nearAi.agent.compactAtTokens.description: Summarize a conversation's earlier history once it reaches this many tokens, whatever the model's context window, and trim old tool output from 80% of it. Smaller transcripts make every turn faster and cheaper. 0 uses only the window-based thresholds.

nearAi.agent.modelStallSeconds.description: A model reply that sends nothing for this many seconds, before its first token or between chunks, is cut and retried once on the backup model (nearAi.agent.backupModel). A reply that keeps streaming is never cut, however long it takes (a 30-minute ceiling still applies to one reply). Without a backup model the reply keeps waiting. 0 turns it off.

nearAi.agent.backupModel.description: The model a stalled reply (nearAi.agent.modelStallSeconds) is retried on, and the first model a team member moves to when its own model is overloaded at NEAR AI or keeps sending nothing. Empty uses the standard tier, then the deep tier. Only a model at least as private as the chat's model (and, for a team member, as its own model) is used.

nearAi.agent.maxOutputTokens.description: Most output tokens (reasoning included) one agent reply may use, never more than the model allows. A reply cut off at the limit is followed by a request to continue more concisely.

nearAi.agent.roleModels.markdownDescription: Model for each agent role: a tier (`deep`, `standard`, `fast`) or a NEAR model ID, by agent name or a `*` pattern. Research and mapping roles read large inputs in parallel, so they default to the cheaper fast tier; bulk fetch and extract roles do too. Planner, plan-checker, verifier, analyst, editor and red-team roles default to the deep tier, because their judgement decides the outcome. A team member's own `model:` line wins, and an agent never uses a model less private than the chat's. A model chosen for this project in Compare Models is used instead of this setting until you clear it there or with SovAI: Clear This Project's Model Choices.

nearAi.mcp.localServerEffects.markdownDescription: A declaration here is your statement that you trust what that server's tools do: the gate does not check each call's arguments against it, so a declared tool runs without asking in Full auto; only declare servers you trust like your own code. By server id, what the tools of an MCP server that runs on this computer (a command, no web address) may do: `"read"`, `{ "workspaceWrite": ["docs/**"] }`, `{ "network": ["api.example.com"] }`. Until a server is declared, its tools that change data ask before every call in every mode, and a tool that says it may delete or reach the open world (MCP's destructiveHint or openWorldHint), or does not say, keeps asking. A declaration that cannot be read is ignored with a warning. Read from your user settings only.

nearAi.team.pollSeconds.description: How often Team Mode checks the team's coordination log, in seconds, while this window is focused. Unfocused windows check every 2 minutes.

nearAi.team.preview.description: Shows Enable Team Mode in the Command Palette. Team Mode is an early preview: until invitations arrive, a team holds only its owner.

nearAi.staff.multiUserPreview.description: Shows the commands for multi-user staff projects in the Command Palette: make a staff project multi-user, invite, join, admit and remove people, and make a single-machine copy. Multi-user staff projects are an early preview: people and clearances in them are declared by the staff lead, not verified.

scripts.test: npm run compile && node scripts/run-tests.mjs dist/test/*.test.js scripts/test/*.test.mjs
scripts.package: npm run compile && npm run sbom && vsce package --no-dependencies --allow-missing-repository --no-rewrite-relative-links
